updates.title: Inventory and preserve BPM Sites source assets
updates.body:
## Goal
Inventory and preserve the original assets used by the published BPM Sites review and recovered `reference-site/` code. Cameron explicitly superseded Figma as the design authority; do not consult Figma for new design decisions. Existing source asset directory names do not invalidate original Sites-used bytes.

## Authoritative sources
- https://bpm-product-design-review.cameron91.chatgpt.site/index.html
- Recovered source commit `2f95c940c42b1bc4152790a83f0f455f66ceaaa4`
- `reference-site/source-provenance.json` and media/crop manifests

## Scope
- Inventory logos, original carton/tube compositions, lifestyle, texture/application media, fonts and video references used in Sites.
- Preserve originals and record source paths, hashes, dimensions, crops and intended template/section usage.
- Record native Files/product-media bindings and fallback behavior separately from historical/source-only assets.
- Preserve source attribution and identify approval/licensing/creator-media decisions.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every candidate asset maps to the Sites source or a documented native-platform addition.
- [ ] Original available imagery is preserved rather than replaced with placeholders or regenerated images.
- [ ] Responsive dimensions/crops are verified in rendered mobile, tablet and desktop layouts.
- [ ] Alt-text intent and decorative media behavior are documented.
- [ ] Optimized delivery retains originals and is verified in native Shopify; historical-hash gaps are explicit.

## Status boundary
Local asset/provenance checks are prepared evidence, not client acceptance, full rendered fidelity or Shopify Files runtime proof. Preserve prior Figma inventory as historical work only; do not require new Figma exports for this Sites objective.

updates.expectedTitle: BPM Shopify redesign — master implementation tracker
updates.title: BPM Shopify redesign — master implementation tracker
updates.body:
## Objective
Recover the published BPM design direction, translate it into a maintainable Shopify theme, preserve current commerce/app behaviour, and make routine editing possible through Shopify rather than AI regeneration.

## Phase 0 — evidence and acceptance
- [ ] #1 Recover and validate published design-review baseline
- [ ] #2 Inventory/preserve authoritative Sites source assets
- [ ] #28 Reconcile Corey feedback and define design acceptance baseline

**Gate:** Do not treat exploratory prototype copy or layouts as production-approved until #28 is satisfied.

## Phase 1 — understand and protect the current store
- [ ] #3 Shopify development/rollback workflow
- [ ] #4 Shopify app/theme integration audit
- [ ] #13 Current template/content/storefront behaviour audit
- [ ] #14 Content model, metafields and merchant editing strategy
- [ ] #15 Theme Check/lint/PR CI

**Gate:** No live-theme editing. Development must have a preview path and rollback plan.

## Phase 2 — theme foundations
- [ ] #5 BPM theme tokens and global chrome
- [ ] #6 Reusable merchant-editable BPM sections

**Gate:** Shared design patterns should exist before page-specific duplication begins.

## Phase 3 — commerce and templates
- [ ] #7 Product-detail template
- [ ] #8 Storefront templates epic
  - [ ] #16 Homepage
  - [ ] #17 Collection/search/product cards
  - [ ] #18 About/Indigenous-owned/Contact/content pages
  - [ ] #19 Blog/article
  - [ ] #20 Cart/search/account/localisation UI
  - [ ] #21 Bundle/subscription/offer presentation

## Phase 4 — hardening
- [ ] #9 Quality hardening epic
  - [ ] #22 SEO/structured data
  - [ ] #23 Accessibility
  - [ ] #24 Performance/Core Web Vitals
  - [ ] #25 Analytics/pixels/events
  - [ ] #29 Product copy/claims/shipping/policy verification

## Phase 5 — QA and release
- [ ] #10 QA/release epic
  - [ ] #26 Cross-device visual/interaction QA
  - [ ] #27 Production release/rollback/post-launch verification

## Non-negotiables
- The existing ChatGPT Site remains unchanged as recovery/reference evidence.
- No production-theme change without explicit approval for that exact action.
- Shopify product/price/availability/selling-plan data must not be hard-coded when Shopify/app data can supply it.
- Corey must be able to edit routine content through Shopify Admin/theme editor.
- App blocks/embeds must remain compatible, including Bundles, Agentic, Google and Judge.me where currently used.
- Mobile, tablet and desktop QA are required.
- Accessibility, SEO, performance, analytics and rollback are part of launch scope, not optional polish.
- Do not invent product, shipping, pricing, ingredient, ownership or performance claims.

## Definition of project done
- [ ] Approved visual direction is represented in Shopify.
- [ ] Current commerce/app functionality has no known blocking regression.
- [ ] Merchant editing is documented and usable without code for routine changes.
- [ ] Required automated/static checks pass.
- [ ] QA evidence exists for representative devices and critical flows.
- [ ] Claims/content are approved/current.
- [ ] Release and rollback have been verified.
- [ ] Production launch has separate explicit approval.

## Canonical planning docs
- [Implementation plan](../blob/recovery/chatgpt-site-baseline/docs/shopify-redesign-plan.md)
- [QA matrix](../blob/recovery/chatgpt-site-baseline/docs/qa-matrix.md)

These documents are currently on the recovery/planning branch and should be reviewed with PR #12 before merge.

## Design-source correction
Cameron explicitly selected https://bpm-product-design-review.cameron91.chatgpt.site/index.html and recovered `reference-site/` code, superseding Figma. Follow `docs/shopify-redesign-plan.md`; preserve recovery and historical work. Source asset folder names may still contain `figma`, but no new Figma design decisions are required.

## Evidence and completion boundaries
Recovery PR #12 is merged. Source retrieval/hash/route checks and local custom-theme checks are distinct evidence; current custom-theme CI, authenticated dev upload, native app/editor/purchase QA, full device/source fidelity, approved claims/offers/policies, client acceptance and controlled production release remain separately gated. Do not close implementation issues from recovery CI or local fixtures alone. Development upload requires the reviewed exact command; production publication requires separate explicit approval.

updates.title: Cross-device visual and interaction QA
updates.body:
## Goal
Systematically test the redesigned theme across representative viewport classes before release.

## Depends on
- All primary template issues
- #23 accessibility
- #24 performance where fixes affect layout

## Representative viewport classes
- Mobile: narrow and large phone
- Tablet: portrait and landscape representative widths
- Desktop: standard laptop and wide desktop

## QA
- Layout/reflow
- Navigation
- Product gallery
- PDP purchase controls
- Cart/cart drawer
- Search
- Forms
- FAQ/accordions
- App blocks
- Long content
- Footer
- Focus/keyboard behaviour
- Touch targets
- Hover-only behaviour
- Broken images/links

## Done when
- [ ] QA evidence is recorded per major template and viewport class.
- [ ] P0/P1 visual or functional regressions are resolved.
- [ ] Remaining lower-priority defects have explicit issues.
- [ ] No template is marked complete based on desktop-only review.

updates.expectedTitle: Production release, rollback and post-launch verification
updates.title: Production release, rollback and post-launch verification
updates.body:
## Goal
Define and execute a reversible launch process only after explicit production approval.

## Depends on
- #10 storefront regression/launch gate
- #25 analytics verification
- #26 cross-device QA
- All blocking app/commerce issues

## Pre-launch
- Confirm approved theme/commit.
- Confirm production backup.
- Confirm unpublished theme preview.
- Re-run required checks.
- Confirm no unapproved scope.
- Record current live theme ID/version.
- Prepare rollback steps.

## Launch
Production theme publication is **not** part of planning approval. It requires explicit approval for that action.

## Post-launch verification
- Homepage/PDP/collection
- Cart/checkout handoff
- Subscription/bundle paths
- Reviews/app blocks
- Search/forms
- Analytics/customer events
- SEO metadata/canonicals
- 404/broken assets
- Mobile smoke test

## Done when
- [ ] Release checklist is complete.
- [ ] Explicit launch approval is recorded.
- [ ] Production publish succeeds.
- [ ] Post-launch smoke checks pass.
- [ ] Rollback path remains available and documented.
- [ ] Any post-launch defect has an issue with severity/owner.
